US_plan_after_observed_night_attack.priority_1: restore and harden Red 2/3 connection and supply-command corridor
US_plan_after_observed_night_attack.priority_2: land remaining Shermans/engineers/ammunition through verified high-water lanes and repair LVT shuttle fleet
US_plan_after_observed_night_attack.priority_3: reduce observed strongpoints with tank + engineer + 75-mm + destroyer/CVE spotting cycle before broad advance
US_plan_after_observed_night_attack.not_assumed: perfect knowledge of every bunker, underground connection or Japanese local ammunition state

US_ground_state.LVT: some D-day damaged vehicles return to shuttle/casualty-evac duty; enough lift exists to improve logistics, but not all 87-wave vehicles are available
US_ground_state.communications: much better than historical 20-Nov Tarawa because dry radios/lanes were achieved, but night damage and congestion still require local rerouting

Japanese_ground_state.organized_first_line_equivalent_at_dawn: ~1650-2050 across strongpoints/local reserves; not all mutually connected
Japanese_ground_state.armed_support_local_pool: ~450-650 useful for strongpoint security, ammunition, local fighting and runners; not equal to SNLF infantry
Japanese_ground_state.Type95_day_use: 2-4 vehicles appear in short-hop/local-firepoint actions; avoid a second mass charge
Japanese_ground_state.Type95_T24: 2-4 contact-capable centered, with 0-1 additional short-repair candidate; recovery ceiling deteriorates as US territory expands
Japanese_ground_state.C2: islandwide command increasingly unreliable; strongpoint-level wire/runners remain materially better than historical baseline
Japanese_ground_state.ammunition: no islandwide shortage yet, but local isolation creates uneven stocks; well-dispersed magazines delay catastrophic local collapse

terrain_progress.morning: Red 2/3 connection restored and armored by roughly 08:30-10:30 centered
terrain_progress.afternoon: US expands over much of the central lagoon-side/airfield sector; advance is deliberate because active south/west-oriented positions can still fire obliquely or counter local moves
terrain_progress.Green_Beach_west: not treated as fully open logistics beach by T24; western positions remain costly and require reduction
terrain_progress.east_north: organized Japanese pockets remain; no secure-island declaration is plausible

casualties.US_cumulative_through_11_25_T24: ~2000-2550 total K/W/M class working band; final campaign tally remains open
casualties.Japan_Dplus1: ~650-900 additional casualties class, heavily concentrated in exposed strongpoints and the remnants of the night mobile reserve

T24_assessment: US beachhead is operationally secure and increasingly well supplied, but Japanese organized defense remains coherent enough to require at least another multi-day reduction effort. The ground clock is now later than v004 and must feed back into naval-air mission state.
